problem: The update divides the sum by B, but the same section says the last batch may be smaller. For that batch the average must divide by the actual number of samples in the batch, not by B. Using 1/B scales the last update of every epoch down by |Bt|/B.
fix: Write θ<sub>t+1</sub> = θ<sub>t</sub> − η · (1/|B<sub>t</sub>|) Σ<sub>i∈B<sub>t</sub></sub> ∇ℓ<sub>i</sub>(θ<sub>t</sub>), and state that |B<sub>t</sub>| = B except possibly for the last batch of an epoch.

where: Section 2, linear scaling heuristic; Quiz Q6
problem: The variance argument alone does not justify multiplying η by k. A batch k times larger makes the gradient's standard deviation √k times smaller, which by itself suggests a √k scaling, not k. The standard justification for the k scaling is that k steps of size η on batches of size B approximate one step of size kη on a batch of size kB. Also, Q6's 'a step k times larger keeps a similar scale of parameter movement' can be read as per-update movement, which is actually k times larger; the similar movement is per epoch, because there are k times fewer updates.
fix: State the k-step approximation: one step of size kη with batch size kB moves the parameters about as far as k steps of size η with batch size B, so progress per epoch is similar. In Q6, say 'each individual update is k times larger, but the movement per epoch stays similar because there are k times fewer updates'.
